jobs.title: Regional Sales Director-Eastern Europe
jobs.description:
About JSSI
Founded in 1989 and headquartered in Chicago, Jet Support Services, Inc. (JSSI) is the largest independent provider of hourly cost maintenance programs for business aviation. JSSI delivers comprehensive coverage for engines, airframes, and auxiliary power units (APUs) across more than 300 different aircraft makes and models, helping owners and operators stabilize maintenance budgets, maximize aircraft availability, and protect asset value throughout the lifecycle of ownership.   JSSI has built a portfolio of complementary business lines designed to simplify the economic and technical complexity of business aviation; these include Maintenance teams, Traxxall maintenance tracking software, Parts & Engines, Conklin aircraft cost and performance data, and Aviation Capital asset-based financing solutions. Together, these offerings support owners, operators, and maintenance providers with integrated tools spanning ownership and maintenance planning, execution, and financial management.   With more than 6,500 aircraft supported through programs and software platforms, JSSI leverages its unique independence, unmatched scale, and data-driven insight to deliver customized solutions and support models aligned to the interests of each client — regardless of aircraft platform. JSSI is backed by leading institutional investors GTCR, Genstar Capital, and Blackstone. Learn more at jetsupport.com. 

Position Summary: 

 

The Regional Sales Director will be responsible for generating sales on JSSI Maintenance Software’s two maintenance tracking platforms.  This position will report into the Chief Commercial Officer of the Maintenance Software division and will work the assigned sales territory to close business.  

 


Duties and Responsibilities:
  • Build and maintain a network of sources from which to identify new sales leads.
  • Process, qualify, and communicate with leads from various sources.
  • Work all aspects of the sales pipeline to ensure consistent production.
  • Perform online demonstrations of JSSI Maintenance Software platforms using Go To Meeting, Zoom, or Microsoft Teams.
  • Generate new sales within assigned sales territory and meet sales quota.
  • Maintain detailed reports of sales activities including calls, closed sales, lost business, and any other pertinent information into Salesforce.com.
  • Identify market trends to anticipate areas of opportunity.
  • Negotiate prices with customers and generate contracts for new and existing customers.
  • Travel within sales territory or to industry tradeshows and events to promote and sell JSSI Maintenance Software services.

Desired Credentials:
  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 5+ years in an aviation sales; preferably in aviation software or aircraft sales.
  • Working knowledge of aircraft and the business aviation industry.
  • Ability to function independently.
  • Ability to cultivate strong relationships and communicate effectively via email and telephone.
  • Experience with Salesforce.com and Jetnet preferred.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, & PowerPoint.

At JSSI, we are committed to rewarding our team members with competitive and comprehensive compensation packages that reflect their contributions and talent.

For this role, the annual base pay generally ranges from €89,180 to €102,557 (EUR), with the final offer determined by variable factors including but not limited to market location, job-specific knowledge, skills, education, and experience. In addition, your total rewards package may include an annual discretionary bonus plan, incentive or sales bonus plan, or other form of additional compensation, based on your role.

Additionally, for full-time employees based in the USA, Canada, or the Philippines, we are proud to offer a robust suite of benefits. This ranges from insurance offerings such as medical, dental, vision, retirement savings programs, among others, starting day one of employment. For a full overview of our offerings, visit the JSSI Benefits Page on our company website.


JSSI is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristic protected by law.

JSSI does not accept unsolicited resumes from individual recruiters or third-party recruiting agencies in response to job postings. No fee will be paid to third parties who submit unsolicited candidates directly to our hiring managers or Recruiting Team.

jobs.title: (Senior) FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Location: Remote (Within +/- 2 hours of CET)

Contract type: Full-time 

Salary: Starting from €70,000 per annum gross, subject to location, skills and experience

Not Your Typical Workplace.…

Tired of the 9-to-5 grind? Imagine a World without borders, where opportunities are endless. That's the future of work, and what we are building at WorkMotion.Our remote-first team spans across the world, helping companies hire, onboard, and manage talent internationally through smart, flexible workforce solutions. Fast-paced, people-driven, and globally connected — we empower businesses to build teams without borders.

More Than a Role…

We don’t just need a (Senior) FP&A Manager  — we need a strategic finance business partner and performance architect.. We’re looking for someone who gets their energy from turning complex financial data into clear insights, challenging assumptions, improving planning discipline, and helping the business make better decisions , while keeping a sharp, analytical focus on how their work delivers real business impact.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to stay in their lane. You’ll be at the center of it all —shaping financial planning, driving forecasting and performance management, influencing strategic decisions, and connecting local business performance with group-level expectations — ensuring everything you touch is accurate, insight-driven, commercially relevant, scalable  and aligned with our wider goals.

You won’t be a solo operator. You’ll collaborate with local and group finance teams, senior leadership, commercial, operational, and functional stakeholders  and external auditors, system implementation partners, and corporate reporting teams , bringing everything together to ensure consistency, impact, and momentum across the board.

Where Responsibility Meets Real Opportunity…

  • Lead annual budgeting, monthly and quarterly forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the business.
  • Translate financial and operational performance into clear insights, variance analysis, risks, opportunities, and recommendations for senior leadership.
  • Partner with commercial, operational, functional, local finance, and group finance teams to support strategic initiatives and improve business performance.
  • Build and maintain robust financial models, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting packages to support decision-making and investment cases.
  • Ensure alignment between local German reporting requirements and group-level expectations within a U.S. publicly listed company environment.
  • Drive continuous improvement across FP&A processes, planning tools, data quality, reporting automation, and performance management routines.

What It Takes to Make an Impact Here…

  • Approximately 7 years of progressive experience in FP&A, controlling, corporate finance, or a related finance function, ideally in an international or matrixed organization.
  • Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modeling, management reporting, variance analysis, and business performance management.
  • Good understanding of relationship between balance sheet, profit and loss account and the cash flow statement.
  • Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with ERP, planning, and reporting tools such as Oracle NetSuite, Oracle Fusion, Power BI, Tableau, Anaplan, Hyperion, OneStream, or similar.
  • Strong commercial mindset, analytical thinking, stakeholder management, and the confidence to challenge assumptions and influence decision-making.
  • Fluent English is required.

Bonus Points If You Bring…

  • Experience preparing board materials, earnings support schedules, management review packs, or group reporting deliverables.
  • Exposure to finance transformation, planning system implementation, BI dashboards, or reporting automation projects.
  • Professional qualification such as MBA, CFA, ACCA, CIMA, or equivalent is a strong asset.
  • Experience in a high-growth, complex, multinational, or publicly listed company environment.

Not Your Typical Team…

We are a team of highly talented Finance and Accounting minds, working across the whole globe. We’re a team of motivated, and fully distributed crew that proves "remote" doesn't mean "disconnected."

We don’t just “work” together — we create, challenge, and grow together. If you’re looking for an environment where your ideas are welcomed, your voice is heard, cross-collaboration on bold strategies thrive on collective brainpower and high-energy teamwork you’ll feel right at home. 

The Perks of Being Here…

  • Global, remote, and thriving:  We're a global team of talented individuals spread across 26 countries. Our WorkFlex program lets you work from anywhere, anytime. Whether it's a beachside office or a cosy home office, the choice is yours.
  • Your well-being is our priority: We know mental health matters, which is why we offer a dedicated Well-Being Day—a full day off just to recharge and relax.
  • Get fit and stay active: Whether it’s yoga, weightlifting, or a quick jog—work out on your terms, at a discount with our subsidised gym memberships.
  • Learn, grow, and develop: We believe in constant growth. With our Training & Development Allowance, you’ll have all the opportunities you need to keep expanding your skills and knowledge. 
  • Stay connected: Take part in exciting annual team meetups!
  • Diversity is our superpower: We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. 

*Benefits vary depending on location due to local laws and regulations.

jobs.title: Marketing Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Über Vestlane

Vestlane ist die Plattform für Onboarding, KYC/AML und Tax Compliance für Private-Market-Fonds. Fondsmanager und Fondsadministratoren in ganz Europa wickeln über Vestlane ihre KYC-, AML- und Zeichnungsprozesse ab, in über 14 Jurisdiktionen und über den gesamten Investor-Lifecycle hinweg. Wir sind zertifiziert und für die regulatorische Realität spannender Akronyme gebaut – von GwG, BaFin, AMLR, RTS, CSSF bis hin zu DORA, RAIF, AIFMD, MiFID uvm.

Du hast schon ein paar Jahre B2B-Marketing gemacht und willst jetzt Kanäle wirklich verantworten statt nur zuzuarbeiten? Du willst die Welt von Venture Capital und Private Equity von innen kennenlernen, ohne selbst in einem Fonds zu sitzen? Du kannst schreiben, denkst in Zielgruppen statt in Posts und findest es reizvoll, aus GwG und CSSF-Rundschreiben Inhalte zu machen, die Compliance-Verantwortliche tatsächlich lesen? Du betreibst Marketing mit KI-Tools und Daten statt mit der Gießkanne? Dann ist diese Rolle für dich!

Als Marketing Manager arbeitest du direkt mit unserem COO zusammen, der Go-to-Market verantwortet, und in enger Abstimmung mit unserem CEO. Du übernimmst die Marketing-Themen, die heute auf seinem Tisch liegen – von Content und SEO über LinkedIn und Newsletter bis Website und Events – und bist nah dran an jeder Entscheidung, die unsere Positionierung bewegt. Kolleg:innen aus Regulatory, Design und Customer Success liefern dir Fachwissen, Grafiken und Kundenstimmen. Echte Verantwortung für eigene Kanäle ab Tag eins, kurze Wege zur Geschäftsführung, keine Agenturschleifen. Dein Arbeitsplatz ist unser Office in Bonn, mit flexiblen Home-Office-Regelungen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Content, der gelesen wird: Du planst und schreibst Blogartikel, Landingpages und Fachbeiträge zu KYC/AML, AMLR, Fondsregulierung und unseren Produktfeatures – auf Deutsch und Englisch, fachlich sauber, verständlich und mit Haltung.

  • SEO und GEO verantworten: Du baust auf unseren bestehenden Rankings auf, entwickelst die Keyword-Strategie weiter und sorgst dafür, dass Vestlane auch dort gefunden wird, wo heute gesucht wird.

  • LinkedIn und Newsletter fahren: Du bespielst die Company Page, bereitest Posts für die Geschäftsführung vor und verantwortest unseren Regulatory- und Product-Newsletter von der Themenplanung bis zum Versand.

  • Website weiterentwickeln: Du pflegst und erweiterst vestlane.com in unserem CMS (Storyblok), briefst Design, testest neue Seiten und misst, was funktioniert.

  • Success Stories und Events: Du sammelst Kundenstimmen gemeinsam mit Customer Success, machst daraus Case Studies und verantwortest das Pre- und Post-Marketing von Events, Webinaren und Partner-Announcements.

  • Die Marketing-Maschine bauen: Du strukturierst Contentplanung, Tracking und Reporting, baust KI-Workflows für Recherche, Entwürfe und Distribution und zeigst mit Zahlen, welche Maßnahmen Pipeline bringen.

Dein Profil

  • 1 bis 3 Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Marketing, idealerweise SaaS, Finanz- oder Legal-/RegTech-Umfeld. Du hast schon mindestens einen Kanal eigenständig verantwortet (Content, SEO, LinkedIn oder Newsletter) und kannst zeigen, was dabei herausgekommen ist.

  • Du schreibst sehr gut auf Deutsch und Englisch: klar, präzise, ohne Buzzword-Nebel. Du kannst einen komplexen Sachverhalt in drei Sätzen erklären und in einem Post zuspitzen.

  • Solide SEO-Kenntnisse (Keyword-Recherche, On-Page, Content-Struktur, Tracking) und echtes Interesse an Generative Engine Optimization. Erfahrung mit einem CMS, LinkedIn Company Pages und einem Newsletter-Tool.

  • Du nutzt KI-Tools im Alltag selbstverständlich für Recherche, Entwürfe und Analysen und weißt, wo du selbst nachschärfen musst.

  • Du magst Zahlen: Du willst wissen, ob dein Artikel rankt, ob der Newsletter geöffnet wird und was davon im CRM ankommt.

  • Interesse an Finanzregulierung und Compliance. Du musst kein GwG-Profi sein, aber du musst Lust haben, dich einzuarbeiten – Fachwissen bekommst du von Kolleg:innen, die täglich damit arbeiten.

  • Du siehst dich als Unternehmer:in innerhalb von Vestlane, nicht als Content-Lieferant:in. Du willst heute Verantwortung und morgen Führung, und du willst dir beides erarbeiten, indem du etwas aufbaust.

Deine Benefits

  • Eigene Kanäle und Themen ab Tag eins, mit klarem Entwicklungspfad hin zu mehr Verantwortung im Marketing

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit COO und CEO, kurze Entscheidungswege, keine Agenturschleifen

  • Vollzeit, unbefristet, Start ab sofort möglich

  • Kompetitives Gehaltspaket

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Bezahlte Weiterbildungen und Zertifizierungen

  • Arbeitsplatz in unserem Bonner Office, flexible Arbeitszeiten und Home-Office-Regelungen

  • Moderne Tools und KI im täglichen Einsatz

  • Ein Team, das Compliance ernst nimmt, weil Compliance das Produkt ist, kein Kostenfaktor

Abschluss

Wir freuen uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und zwei bis drei Arbeitsproben (Artikel, Posts, Landingpages, Newsletter – was zeigt, wie du arbeitest). Ein klassisches Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht; ein paar Sätze dazu, warum Marketing für ein RegTech dich reizt, reichen. Wir prüfen deine Bewerbung persönlich und melden uns innerhalb von zwei Wochen.

Der Prozess ist bewusst kurz und hat drei Schritte: ein 30-minütiges Kennenlerngespräch, in dem es um dich, deinen Weg und die Frage geht, ob wir zueinander passen. Dann ein 45-minütiger Termin mit einer praktischen Aufgabe aus dem echten Alltag – zum Beispiel ein LinkedIn-Post zu einem regulatorischen Thema –, damit du siehst, was dich erwartet, und wir sehen, wie du arbeitest. Zum Abschluss ein 30-minütiges Gespräch mit der Geschäftsführung. Insgesamt weniger als zwei Stunden deiner Zeit, und du bekommst nach jedem Schritt zeitnah Rückmeldung.

Fragen vor der Bewerbung? Melde dich bei uns!

jobs.title: Founders Associate – Operations (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Über Vestlane und die Rolle

Vestlane ist die Plattform für Onboarding, KYC/AML und Tax Compliance für Private-Market-Fonds. Fondsmanager und Fondsadministratoren in ganz Europa wickeln über Vestlane ihre KYC-, AML- und Zeichnungsprozesse ab, in über 14 Jurisdiktionen und über den gesamten Investor-Lifecycle hinweg. Wir sind zertifiziert und für die regulatorische Realität spannender Akronyme gebaut – von GwG, BaFin, AMLR, RTS, CSSF bis hin zu DORA, RAIF, AIFMD, MiFID uvm.

Du willst sehen, wie ein B2B-SaaS-Unternehmen wirklich funktioniert – nicht aus der Folie, sondern aus dem Maschinenraum? Du willst die Welt von Venture Capital und Private Equity von innen kennenlernen, ohne den Umweg über drei Jahre Investment Banking? Du baust lieber einen Prozess, der ein Problem dauerhaft löst, als es jede Woche neu zu lösen? Du arbeitest mit KI-Tools und Automatisierung so selbstverständlich wie andere mit Excel? Dann ist diese Rolle für dich!

Als Founders Associate arbeitest du direkt mit unserem COO zusammen, der Operations und Go-to-Market verantwortet. Du übernimmst die operativen Themen, die heute auf seinem Tisch liegen – von Prozessen und Tooling über Finance und Compliance bis HR – und bist nah dran an jeder Entscheidung, die das Unternehmen bewegt. Echte Verantwortung ab Tag eins, direkter Draht zu Steuerberatung, Dienstleistern und Partnern, und ein Überblick über ein wachsendes SaaS-Unternehmen, den dir kein Konzern bietet. 2–3 Tage pro Woche arbeitet ihr gemeinsam vor Ort im Raum Erfurt/Weimar, an einem Arbeitsplatz, den du von Anfang an mit aufbaust; den Rest flexibel aus dem Home-Office.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Die interne Maschine bauen (dein Schwerpunkt): Du dokumentierst, standardisierst und automatisierst unsere internen Abläufe – von einem Wiki, das tatsächlich gelesen wird, über KI-Agenten für wiederkehrende Aufgaben bis zur Verwaltung unserer Tool- und Vendorlandschaft (Verträge, Zugänge, Kosten). Du erkennst, wo wir Zeit verlieren, und beseitigst die Ursache.

  • Entscheidungen vorbereiten: Du baust Analysen und Entscheidungsvorlagen für COO und CEO – Unit Economics, Markt- und Wettbewerbsrecherchen, Investorenreporting – und lieferst Zahlen statt Meinungen.

  • Finance und Accounting unterstützen: Du übernimmst die vorbereitende Buchhaltung, prüfst und stellst Rechnungen, bereitest Zahlungsläufe vor, arbeitest unserer Steuerberatung zu und hältst Kosten- und Liquiditätsübersichten aktuell.

  • Compliance-Operations am Laufen halten: Du pflegst Nachweise und Richtlinien für ISO 27001 und SOC 2, bereitest Audits vor und hältst unsere Subprozessorenliste und Fristen in Ordnung.

  • Hiring und HR mittragen: Du schreibst Stellenanzeigen, screenst Bewerbungen, koordinierst Interviews und sorgst dafür, dass neue Kolleg:innen sauber onboarded werden – von Arbeitsvertrag und Equipment bis zum ersten Tag. Daneben hältst du unsere HR-Prozesse und -Tools in Ordnung.

  • Verträge und Angebote im Griff behalten: Du bereitest Angebote vor, hältst unsere Pipeline in Salesforce aktuell und behältst Kunden-, Partner- und Auftragsverarbeitungsverträge im Blick – Versionen, Fristen, Unterschriften.

Dein Profil

  • Abgeschlossenes Studium (z. B. BWL, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Wirtschaftsrecht oder vergleichbar) oder eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung. Ob frisch von der Uni oder mit ein bis zwei Jahren Erfahrung aus Startup, Beratung oder Finanzbranche: Praktika und Werkstudententätigkeiten zählen, Haltung zählt mehr.

  • Sehr sicher in Excel/Google Sheets, strukturiert in Dokumentation und Projektmanagement. Erfahrung mit Salesforce, Buchhaltungs- oder Automatisierungstools (z. B. Zapier, Make, n8n) ist ein Plus.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI-Tools (Claude, ChatGPT o. ä.) nicht nur zum Texten, sondern um Prozesse zu bauen – und du weißt, wo du selbst prüfen musst.

  • Fließendes Deutsch und gutes Englisch – Partner, Dienstleister und Teile des Teams arbeiten auf Englisch.

  • Präzision und Pragmatismus: Du arbeitest selbstständig, fragst nach, wenn etwas unklar ist, und weißt, wann es auf jedes Detail ankommt – und wann nicht.

  • Du hast kein Problem damit, morgens eine Rechnung zu prüfen und nachmittags ein Bewerbungsgespräch zu organisieren. Breite ist für dich kein Mangel an Fokus, sondern die Chance, das ganze Unternehmen zu verstehen und zu Lernen.

  • Interesse an Fonds, Finanzregulierung oder Compliance ist willkommen, Vorwissen keine Voraussetzung – das bringen wir dir bei.

  • Du siehst dich als Unternehmer:in innerhalb von Vestlane, nicht als Zuarbeiter:in. Du willst heute Verantwortung und morgen Führung, und du willst dir beides erarbeiten, indem du etwas aufbaust.

Vorteile

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit COO und CEO, keine fünf Ebenen zwischen dir und den Entscheidungen

  • Vollzeit, unbefristet, Start ab sofort möglich

  • Kompetitives Gehaltspaket

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

Quandela stands as a global leader in quantum computing, driven by groundbreaking technology and a strategic vision for scaling quantum solutions. Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀 

Description of the Team/Project

One of Quandela's priority is demonstrating fault tolerant quantum computing. We are widely known for our boson samplers, where one source can provide many photons, but for FTQC we will do spin-spin operations, mediated by photons with a dash of entanglement. So, instead of many photons from few sources, we need many photons from many spins. That means that someone has to ; every day, for months ; test many "spin-photon sources" together and determine whether the photons have adequate properties (single, indistinguishable, entangled), and other things. Where you will help, is making these measurements less tedious, by making some of it automated. For instance, by rotating waveplates by the right amount and in the right order at the right time. Upon your arrival the setup should be already built, but if we are behind schedule, you will probably give a hand on that too.

  • Zahlen verantworten. Deine KPIs entlang des Funnels, gemeinsam mit unserem Commercial Engine Lead, der Tracking und Infrastruktur baut.
  • Sales-Enablement-Material. Du passt an, was zum Verkaufen und Vermarkten in der Schweiz am besten wirkt, von Sprache bis Preisdarstellung in CHF.

Dein Profil

Must-have

  • Echte Hunter-Mentalität. Du hast bereits aktiv Erstkontakte am Telefon gemacht und hast damit kein Problem. Wenn dich 40 Gespräche am Tag abschrecken, ist das die falsche Rolle
  • Kenntnis des Schweizer Gesundheitswesens oder die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell einzuarbeiten: Grundversicherung, Anordnungsmodell, Rolle von Kantonen und Verbänden
  • Glaubwürdigkeit gegenüber Therapeut:innen. Psychotherapeut:innen vertrauen vor allem Psychotherapeut:innen. Entweder bringst du diesen Hintergrund mit, oder du arbeitest dich so schnell und so tief ein, dass man es dir im Gespräch nicht anmerkt

  • Kommunikationsstärke mit Abschlussfokus. Empathisch und auf Augenhöhe, denn Psychotherapeut:innen merken sofort, wenn jemand verkauft, statt zu verstehen

Von Vorteil

  • Vertriebserfahrung mit Praxen, Heilberufen oder Spitälern in der Schweiz

Was wir bieten

  • Einen Markt, den du prägst. Du bist die erste Person von VIA in der Schweiz. Was du aufbaust, wird zum Fundament unseres Schweizer Geschäfts
  • Ein Team, das überperformt. DACH-Marktführer für KI-Assistenz in der Psychotherapie in zwei Jahren, bootstrapped. Unsere Pläne von hier sind deutlich grösser, und wir stellen Menschen ein, die das mitgestalten wollen

  • Sinnstiftende Arbeit. Jede Praxis, die du gewinnst, bedeutet mehrere Stunden pro Woche, die wieder Patient:innen zugutekommen
  • Flexibel arbeiten. Remote aus der Schweiz, freie Zeiteinteilung, moderne Ausstattung und regelmässige Teamtage in unserem Büro in Berlin-Mitte

Wir suchen keine:n klassische:n Vertriebler:in, sondern eine:n Macher:in, die oder der mit Hunger und Hands-on-Mentalität VIA in der Schweiz zur ersten Wahl macht.

  • Operate and scale specialized infrastructure for demanding workloads, including GPU clusters for computer vision models, media engines, and data analytics platforms 
  • Evolve our observability stack to proactively monitor system health, define meaningful alerting, and ensure high availability
  • Drive platform security and compliance through continuous vulnerability scanning, automated image screening, robust secrets management, and strict access controls
  • Collaborate closely with software engineers, data scientists, and product teams to design scalable architectures and act as a strategic technical partner for new infrastructure initiatives 

Help define technical direction, engineering best practices, and quality standards within the infrastructure domain 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 5+ years of professional experience in DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering, or Platform Engineering, with a proven track record of designing and scaling highly available production environments 
  • Strong hands-on experience running Kubernetes in production, including upgrades, networking and troubleshooting
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure (AWS) combined with experience operating bare-metal or self-hosted environments

Proven experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible) and modern container build or GitOps workflowsStrong problem-solving skills and the ability to evaluate technical trade-offs between reliability, scalability, and maintainabilityExperience collaborating across engineering and product teams to deliver secure and robust infrastructure solutionsDeep understanding of Linux operating systems and strong programming or scripting skills (e.g., Python, Go, or Bash) focused on automation and tooling. 

Nice to have – and what would make you exceptional:

  • Experience operating GPU workloads on Kubernetes or Machine Learning infrastructure
  • Familiarity with specialized Kubernetes ecosystem tools such as FluxCD, Rancher, or RKE2.
  • Experience working with large-scale video/streaming workflows or AWS media services
  • Experience managing and scaling messaging or event-streaming systems (e.g., Kafka) 
  • Experience operating and optimizing relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) 
  • Experience building internal developer platforms or self-service tooling for engineering teams

This position is remote-friendly.

The Legal team is at the heart of Joko’s growth and protection. We navigate the complexities of contracts, regulations, and risk management to ensure the company operates smoothly and seizes opportunities with confidence.

We handle all legal matters: Contracts, Corporate, Labor, Data protection, IP etc… enabling other teams to innovate with confidence.

Leveraging our expertise and external partners, we collaborate with all functions to protect Joko’s interests efficiently and proactively.

🚀 What you will do

As Legal Counsel, Commercial & IP, you will work hand in hand with our business teams to negotiate the partnerships that drive Joko's growth, and you will own our contracts, IP, commercial disputes and insurance. You will report directly to the Head of Legal (Maya).

🛡️ IP and technology

  • Define the legal framework for Juno, our AI shopping assistant: our rights to merchant content and catalogue data, the use of third-party brands and logos in the app and our marketing, and the ownership of AI-generated content.

  • Protect the Joko brands across our markets with our IP counsel, from trademarks, domain names, oppositions and renewals to action against third parties that infringe our rights.

  • Work with Product and Marketing to secure new features and brands before they launch.

🤝 Deals and commercial relationships

  • Sit alongside the business teams in their negotiations with merchants and brands: partnership agreements, data-sharing contracts, CPG and B2B deals, and the contracts for our new business lines.

  • Structure our merchant and brand relationships so they hold up under French and EU rules on restrictive commercial practices, including significant imbalance and the abrupt termination of established commercial relationships.

  • Lead or support the negotiation of contracts on exclusivity, most-favoured-nation, competition law risks and parity clauses.

  • Build the templates, playbooks, red lines and fallback positions the business teams use every day, and turn them into AI skills.

⚖️ Disputes and risk

  • Handle disputes with merchants, partners and suppliers together with the teams who own the relationship, from formal notices to settlement, protecting both our position and the relationship.

  • Brief and manage our litigation counsel when a dispute goes to court.

  • Own our insurance programme (D&O, cyber, travel and any new line), from renewals to claims, and build an international programme with our brokers so coverage follows us into each new country.

🙌 Who you are

  • You have 4 to 6 years of experience in commercial or IP/IT law, including time in a top-tier law firm. In-house experience in a tech or consumer company is a strong plus.

  • You have negotiated complex commercial agreements directly with counterparties, in French and in English, and you enjoy it.

  • Experience in commercial disputes, restrictive commercial practices or IP/IT matters related to AI is a strong plus.

  • You understand how a business makes money, and you use the contract to support it rather than to slow it down.

  • You turn your positions into templates and playbooks that non-lawyers can use on their own.

  • You hold a Master's degree in business law, IP/IT law or contract law from a leading French law school. Admission to the Paris Bar is a plus.

  • You are fluent in French and English. Another European language is a plus.

  • You write clearly, you decide with incomplete information, and you like the pace of a scale-up.

  • You are curious about AI and want to learn how to build the tools that change legal work.

What we tell you upfront. Until the three poles are staffed, every Legal Counsel works across the full legal scope with the Head of Legal. Functional ownership is formalised as soon as the Commercial & IP and Product & Privacy seats are both filled.

💎 Our perks

(Some of the benefits listed below are available to full-time positions only)

At Joko, we believe that flexibility and trust are essential. Our work environment reflects this through:

  • Flexible remote : If you live in Paris, you can choose to work from our office or from home with no constraints. If you live elsewhere, we can provide access to a coworking space and a coworking budget.

  • Work from anywhere : Want to spend a month in Italy while working? You can work from most countries in the world for up to 3 months per year.

On top of that, we offer plenty of perks:

  • 💸 Top-market compensation

  • 📈 Equity for everyone with the chance to own a piece of what you build

  • 🤖 Half-day each week dedicated to leveling up with AI by exploring new tools, iterating hard, and sharpening your skills

  • 🌴 Yearly offsite in amazing locations and budget for team-building events & monthly in-person gatherings

  • 💪 Contribution to your ClassPass subscription

  • 🍼 8-week leave paid 100% for the second parent

  • …and much more, check the full list here!

🤝 Our hiring process

  1. Intro call: Quick screening with the Hiring Manager or the Talent team.

  2. Step 1 – Team interview (45 min): Conversation with two Joko team members (could include the Hiring Manager, people from the team you’d join, or colleagues from other teams).

  3. Step 2 – Role-specific assessments

    • For non-engineering roles: A take-home case study followed by a 45-min interview. We assess both your output and how you think in real time. The exercise will be relevant to your role (e.g. analysis, strategy, or process design).

    • For engineering roles: A 90-min live technical interview on CoderPad covering code understanding, review, system design, and product thinking (with AI serving as a collaboration tool).

  4. Step 3 – Leadership interview (45 min): Conversation with a SteerCo member and a Founder.

  5. References: Up to 3 calls with former colleagues or managers.

We’re in our Munich office four days a week, with 100+ people building together every day. We measure outcomes. Trust is high and feedback is direct. We offer competitive salary and meaningful equity.

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. Your Profile

  2. Hiring Manager Interview (45 min)

  3. On-site day: a case with three Builders and Pool Leads (1 hour), Meet the Team (30 min)

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

About the role
Legora is building the AI-native workspace for legal work, with lawyers. Our Legal Engineers are lawyers who help the world's leading firms turn AI into real change in how they practise. France is one of our fastest-growing markets, and we have just opened our Paris office.
We are looking for a Team Lead to lead our Legal Engineering team for law firms in France. This is a player-coach role: you will lead and develop a team of Legal Engineers while personally running our most strategic firm engagements. You will report to the Director of Legal Engineering, South EMEA.

What you'll be doing

  • Leading the team day to day: priorities, 1:1s, coaching, quality review, capacity and escalations.

  • Hiring, onboarding and developing Legal Engineers, and setting the standard of excellence for the team.

  • Personally leading high-value engagements, from discovery and pilots to firm-wide rollouts, with managing partners, practice heads, innovation and IT teams.

  • Turning commercial priorities into execution with our Go-To-Market and Engagement teams: pilots that convert, rollouts that stick, renewals and expansions.

  • Building relationships at partner and management level, and designing sponsor and champion models inside firms.

  • Turning what works into reusable methods: playbooks, templates, French-language content and training.

  • Being the voice of French law firms inside Legora, bringing evidenced product feedback to our Product team.

  • Representing Legora in the French legal market, on AI and the future of legal practice.

What you bring

  • A strong legal background, typically 8+ years of experience in sophisticated law-firm practice, ideally at counsel or senior associate level in a top-tier firm.

  • Proven people management: you have hired, coached, given hard feedback and managed performance.

  • Commercial acumen: you understand how firms make money, how partners decide and how firms buy, and you can tie your work to business outcomes.

  • Credibility with senior lawyers: you can run a difficult workshop with partners and lead an executive readout.

  • Real fluency with generative AI: you use it, you test it, you know where it fails and you can explain why.

  • Structure without bureaucracy, and the energy to build in a fast-growing team.

  • Native or bilingual French and fluent English.

Strong pluses

  • Experience in legal innovation, knowledge management, legal tech or legal AI.

  • A track record of building something: a practice, a team, a function or a company.

  • A visible voice in the French legal community.

A few more things
You will join a company that moves fast, with a lot of autonomy and real ownership of how Legal Engineering grows in France. We care about Lean In, Fight for Excellence and Grow Together. If that sounds exciting rather than daunting, we'd love to hear from you.

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. jobs.title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Remote)
jobs.description:
This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here

The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.

What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do

You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

  • Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

  • Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

  • Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

  • Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

  • Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

  • Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

  • You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

  • At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

  • You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

  • You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

  • You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

  • You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

  • You make things simpler over time, not more clever

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home

  • You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you

  • You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

Our stack

Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Remote within the EU or EEA

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive compensation

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

  • Training and fine-tuning: embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

  • Document understanding: models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

  • Product matching: retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

  • Evaluation: offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

  • Training and serving infrastructure: automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

  • Customer problems: when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

  • There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

  • You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

  • A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

  • Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

  • You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

  • You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

  • You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

  • You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

  • You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

  • You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

  • You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you.

  • You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is.

  • You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title.

  • Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going.

  • You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls.

  • You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

You probably won't enjoy it if

  • You just want to code and go home.

  • You don't like talking to customers.

  • Ambiguity and chaos bother you.

  • You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you.

  • You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

  • Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Our stack

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

  1. Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

  2. Technical deep-dive call: walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production.

  3. Meet Scalera Day: come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team.

  4. Offer: if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

  • Zürich HQ, four days in the office, Fridays remote. If not located in Zürich then this role is open to remote within the EU or EEA,

  • Occasional customer visits across Switzerland, Austria and Germany

  • Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer II
jobs.description:
Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

We create the technology that redefines utilities and unlocks a new energy system of the future. By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

Please submit your application in English

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In Germany, home to the largest electricity market in Europe and a roadmap toward Net Zero by 2045, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. We are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As we expand our footprint in Germany and the wider European market, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we enter a stage of rapid commercialisation and customer growth in Germany, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll work closely with our engineering team based in Manchester as we look to expand our engineering and operations in Germany and across Europe. Together, the team takes an integration project from the very early information stage, designs how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turns that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

The Gateway (Kraken’s IoT Edge Hardware & Software) and other connectivity technologies with their protocol engineering are owned by our UK-based team, who will support you in becoming configuration literate. Over time you will carry out configuration, deployments and testing for sites yourself, and feed back what you learn about hardware, connectivity and grid operator requirements for European countries so the wider team can build on it.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing, they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing ones.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches for German sites, mainly BESS (grid-scale and C&I) and RES (Wind and Solar). When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives in German and English through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Market access & prequalification support: Support the technical work needed for assets to enter ancillary-service markets (FCR, aFRR, mFRR) and to meet Redispatch 3.0 requirements. With guidance from senior engineers, help prepare the telemetry and control evidence for prequalification (Präqualifikation) with the relevant TSO. (Grid-code and plant-compliance obligations such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120 remain with the plant/PPC; our focus is enabling market access, telemetry and dispatch.)

  • Technical judgement: Develop your technical judgement, making well-reasoned decisions and trade-offs with support from senior engineers, and contributing technical input to discussions within the team.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include German grid connection rules and TSO-specific requirements, ancillary services, Redispatch 3.0, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

  • Gateway application & configuration: Learn how the Gateway software (developed by an internal software team) works and how it is configured. Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the Gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get Gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and software deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing of sites with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Hardware handling & dispatch: Berlin is planned as our stock base for our hardware going out to sites across Europe, so the role includes some hands-on work. This covers preparing units before they ship, such as flashing and configuring our industrial PCs and running pre-shipment tests, and helping to prepare and coordinate shipments.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning, initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand in Germany and other parts of Europe grows. Hardware is deployed remotely in most cases via O&Ms and third parties, but occasional hands-on support in Germany may be needed before or after a deployment.

  • Incidents & support: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Language: Native or professional fluency in German and English, needed for technical documentation and for working with customers, grid operators and our UK-based team.

  • Understanding of the German connection landscape: Working knowledge of the TSO/DSO hierarchy, the connection/integration process, and the technical connection rules (such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120) a grid-connected asset must meet before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the German energy markets: Working understanding of the German ancillary services (FCR, aFRR, mFRR), what prequalification involves, and the Redispatch 3.0 framework.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Hands-on hardware preparation: Comfortable working at the bench with our panels and industrial PCs. This includes safely powering panels up and down using our test setup, flashing operating system images, and following a set procedure for pre-shipment checks. Full training is provided.

  • Industrial communication protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, diagrams and tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with a team that is partly based in another country.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Location and travel: Ideally based close to Kraken’s Berlin office. Willingness to travel to customers and sites in Germany, and occasionally to our Manchester team, although travel is kept to a minimum. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of German grid compliance (VDE-AR-N 4110/4120, TSO-specific technical requirements) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (NIS2, EnWG/KRITIS awareness; IEC 62443 a plus).

  • Exposure to the wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks beyond Germany.

jobs.title: Product Engineer (Frontend) (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Hi, we are Particula, the prime rating provider for digital assets! Our mission? To make the market for digital assets more accessible, secure and transparent for institutional investors. We support issuers, trading facilities, banks and asset managers to create trust, minimize risks and allocate capital effectively. Join our team and shape the future of the financial world with us!

👋 About the Role

We are looking for a product engineer to own our user-facing applications end to end. We operate without dedicated designers or product managers. You will work directly with internal and external stakeholders as well as backend & AI engineers to turn high-level goals into shipped, well-measured features.

This is not a ticket-closing role. You spot user friction, propose a fix, build it, measure the outcome and iterate quickly.

You will also help shape how we build software with AI agents, translating requirements into working code and establishing the guardrails, automated tests and review habits that keep quality high when code is AI-assisted. You remain responsible for every line you ship, whether you or an agent wrote it.

What you will do

  • Ship features end to end: Take concepts from conversation to production, covering UX design, frontend implementation, API integration and deployment.

  • Act as a product builder: Spot friction points yourself, pitch improvements and make sure every feature solves a real user need.

  • Make decisions with data: Implement analytics, track feature adoption and iterate on the numbers.

  • Work directly with users: Talk to internal teams as well as external stakeholders, and turn unstructured feedback into clear technical plans.

  • Own AI-assisted delivery: Use and orchestrate coding agents daily. Write the specs and plans, choose the patterns and approach, and review generated code before you push it.

  • Review your peers' work: Be one of the main reviewers of frontend pull requests, and keep a balance between delivering working functionality and keeping the review workload manageable.

  • Own the design system: Maintain and extend the shared component library and UI guidelines so the product stays consistent. An external design agency will help set the visual language.

  • Own quality and testing: Propose and set up the QA and testing strategy for your area, using automated E2E and component tests to ensure reliability, performance and security.

How we work

These are fixed parts of the job, and we ask candidates to read them as requirements.

  • Delivery process: Work follows a defined delivery process. Inside it, you own the open decisions in your area, including solution design and implementation approach.

  • Decision rights: Architecture, API contracts and design system direction are set centrally because they are shared across teams. You change them through a written proposal. Once a decision is made, everyone follows it. Backend engineers own the security and performance of services.

  • Team rhythm: A daily stand-up and a biweekly Friday demo. Attendance is expected.

  • Speed: We ship small and often and iterate on the interface quickly. Quality comes from tests and reviews, not from polishing before release.

Requirements

Must have

  • 5+ years of commercial software engineering, with evidence of owned product work: features you took from problem to production and measured. Experience in a fast-paced startup is a plus.

  • Strong frontend expertise: Deep proficiency in TypeScript and a modern component framework (Vue 3 / Nuxt preferred).

  • Product and UX sense: A track record of designing clean, functional interfaces and delivering features without dedicated PMs or designers.

  • Data-driven mindset: Hands-on experience setting up and using analytics tools (PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel or similar).

  • Daily use of AI coding agents: Active experience with agentic tools (Claude Code, Copilot), a clear method for guiding them, and a clear method for checking what they produce.

  • Testing and review habits: Experience with automated E2E and UI testing (Playwright, Cypress, Vitest), the ability to define a testing strategy, and the discipline to review code, yours and others', before it merges.

  • Clear communication: Fluent written and spoken English, comfortable presenting ideas to non-technical stakeholders and working through written proposals.

Strong plus

  • Domain background: Prior experience in fintech, Web3 / digital assets or data-driven products.

  • Design systems: Experience building or maintaining a component library.

  • Backend / BFF capability: Experience building APIs and BFF layers, ideally with PHP / Laravel.

  • Cloud and DevOps: Practical experience with AWS environments, deployments and observability.

  • AI tooling workflow: Experience creating agent skills or CI guardrails for AI-assisted development.

Our stack

TypeScript · Vue 3 · Nuxt · PHP · Laravel · AWS · AI-assisted development workflows

Benefits

  • Offsites with the team in exciting locations

  • Flexible working hours in a company that relies on remote work

  • Exciting product in a very dynamic market environment as well as founding-level ownership of a key growth function.

  • Values-based start-up culture

  • Many opportunities to develop further and network with committed people

  • Flat hierarchy

We're a hybrid company building our core development team in Europe around Central European Time. The goal is to establish a hub around Munich, Germany.

Let’s build the next layer of trust for digital assets - together!

Die TeGA-PLAN Heidemann GmbH ist ein unabhängiges Ingenieurbüro für Technische Gebäudeausrüstung mit Sitz in Kiel. Mit rund 30 Kolleginnen und Kollegen planen und begleiten wir spannende und anspruchsvolle Bauprojekte – von der ersten Idee bis zur fertigen Umsetzung.

Unsere Schwerpunkte liegen in der Heizungs-, Lüftungs-, Sanitär- und Elektrotechnik sowie der Gebäudeautomation. Dabei sind unsere Projekte so vielfältig wie unser Team: Ob Forschungs- und Laborgebäude, Gesundheitseinrichtungen, Wohnungsbau, Büro- und Verwaltungsgebäude oder komplexe Industrieanlagen – wir entwickeln technische Lösungen für unterschiedlichste Anforderungen.

Was uns antreibt? Technik sinnvoll einsetzen, statt sie unnötig kompliziert zu machen. Wir legen Wert auf durchdachte, wirtschaftliche und energieeffiziente Lösungen und verfolgen dabei einen klaren Grundsatz: So viel Technik wie nötig, so wenig wie möglich.

Als unabhängiges Ingenieurbüro setzen wir auf fachliche Kompetenz, kurze Entscheidungswege und ein kollegiales Miteinander. Bei uns zählt nicht nur, was wir gemeinsam erreichen, sondern ganz besonders auch, wie wir miteinander arbeiten!

Deine Aufgaben - hier gestaltest du mit:

  • Du bringst unsere Planungen in die Praxis: Als Bauleiter (m/w/d) begleitest du anspruchsvolle Projekte der Heizungs-, Lüftungs- und Sanitärtechnik und sorgst dafür, dass aus guten Konzepten funktionierende Anlagen werden.

  • Du kennst das Baustellenleben: Du bringst Erfahrung in der Bauleitung oder Objektüberwachung mit, weißt, worauf es bei der Umsetzung ankommt, und findest auch dann Lösungen, wenn es mal nicht nach Plan läuft.

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung: Du arbeitest eigenständig, triffst Entscheidungen und vertrittst deine Standpunkte mit fachlicher Kompetenz und einem sicheren Auftreten – ohne dabei das partnerschaftliche Miteinander aus den Augen zu verlieren.

Was dich bei uns erwartet:

Wir finden, dass gute Arbeit auch ein gutes Arbeitsumfeld verdient. Deshalb setzen wir auf Vertrauen, Flexibilität und ein Miteinander, bei dem sich alle wohlfühlen können.

  • Arbeiten, wie es zu deinem Leben passt: Flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice geben dir den Freiraum, den du brauchst.

  • Gut ausgestattet und mobil: Firmenwagen, Smartphone und Laptop gehören ebenso dazu wie die Möglichkeit zum Bike-Leasing und Zuschüsse für öffentliche Verkehrsmittel.

  • Gemeinsam wachsen: Wir unterstützen deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung durch Fortbildungen, gegenseitigen Wissensaustausch und die Erfahrung deiner Kolleginnen und Kollegen.

  • Wohlfühlen statt Kleiderordnung: Bei uns zählt, was du kannst, nicht was du trägst. Dich erwarten ein barrierefreies Büro, kostenlose Getränke und Snacks. Auch vierbeinige Begleiter sind willkommen.

  • Mehr als nur ein Arbeitsplatz: Mit Fitnessangeboten, Mitarbeitervorteilen und gemeinsamen Teamevents sorgen wir dafür, dass auch abseits der Projekte etwas geboten wird.

  • Ein Team, das zusammenhält: Kurze Wege, offene Türen, ein unkomplizierter Umgang miteinander und Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die sich gegenseitig unterstützen, gehören bei uns einfach dazu.

Deine Erfahrung ist uns etwas wert!

Bei uns erwartet dich ein Jahresgehalt zwischen 60.000 und 85.000 € brutto – abhängig von deiner Qualifikation, deiner Erfahrung und der Verantwortung, die du übernimmst. Was du mitbringst, zählt – und das soll sich auch in deinem Gehalt widerspiegeln.

Dein Start bei uns – gemeinsam von Anfang an!

Wir lassen dich nicht ins kalte Wasser springen. Du lernst unser Team, unsere Arbeitsweise und unsere spannenden Projekte in Kiel und Umgebung kennen. Dabei stehen dir erfahrene Kolleginnen und Kollegen zur Seite, die dich bei deinem Einstieg unterstützen.

Schritt für Schritt übernimmst du Verantwortung für deine eigenen Baustellen und wirst Teil eines Teams, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt und gemeinsam Lösungen findet.

Du erfüllst nicht jede Anforderung? Kein Problem! Für uns zählen nicht nur Zeugnisse und Lebensläufe, sondern vor allem deine Erfahrung, deine Persönlichkeit und die Lust, gemeinsam mit uns etwas zu bewegen. Wenn du glaubst, dass du zu uns passt, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager | Integrations & AI Foundations (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
bunch is building the backbone of private markets. We are enabling next-gen fund operations with one integrated system that combines secure data infrastructure, AI-powered workflows and expert fund services. If you value ownership, growth through real responsibility, and working with a thoughtful, ambitious team, this role might be for you.

Your Role

As Senior Product Manager for Integrations & AI Foundations, you're the product owner for bunch's integration and AI platform. You have two kinds of customers: external developers and fund-manager teams connecting to bunch, and the internal product teams building on top of what this team provides.

Integrations & AI Foundations is a new platform squad. It owns the infrastructure that lets data move securely between bunch and other systems, and lets every other product team build AI capabilities — extraction, retrieval, agents and evaluations — without each one solving the same hard problems again.

The team covers five connected areas:

  • Integrations / API layer — API contracts, authentication, versioning and deprecation, rate limits, uptime and SLA, and a Developer Portal

  • MCP layer — agent-callable tools built as thin wrappers over the same API contracts, including a customer-facing MCP offering

  • Document Parsing — a reusable ingestion, decomposition and extraction pipeline, with human-in-the-loop review and accuracy monitoring

  • Retrieval / RAG — chunking, embedding, vector store and retrieval, with access control enforced on every query, offered as a callable service

  • AI Agentic Layer — the agent framework, memory, guardrails, evaluation harness, observability and agent registry other teams use to ship their own agents

Document extraction, agent workflows, evaluations and multi-provider model fallback under EU data residency are already in production.

Fund managers don't want to retype data that already lives in their own systems, and they want to pull their bunch data into their own tools and their own AI. Customers and prospects ask for APIs, CRM and accounting syncs, automated exports of capital accounts, and MCP access.

You'll turn those signals into a coherent platform: one that customers integrate with, and that our own product teams build on, instead of a string of one-off builds.

You will:

  • Set platform strategy and sequencing across the five areas: decide how to slice the work and what ships first

  • Run APIs as a product: contracts, versioning and deprecation policy, rate limits, SLAs, Developer Portal and documentation, and time-to-integrate as a measure you actively drive down

  • Define and launch the customer-facing MCP offering: which capabilities get exposed, tool descriptions that agents actually invoke correctly, and a security review gate for anything customers touch

  • Generalise document parsing: the first use case is already live; your goal will be to take it over and generalise it so more teams can reuse its logic

  • Shape retrieval and the agentic layer as services other teams consume, with access control, guardrails, evaluations and observability built in rather than bolted on

  • Draw and hold ownership lines with domain teams. When a request doesn't map to a named responsibility, run the scoping conversation rather than absorbing it

  • Own platform-wide policy with Engineering and Security: data classification and residency, LLM cost and rate governance, and an integration and extraction registry so nothing gets built twice

  • Work directly with customers — fund managers, CFOs and their technical teams — and with Customer Success to understand integration needs, then turn them into platform decisions

  • Define success through goals and key results and clear metrics per area: API uptime and SLA, time-to-integrate, MCP adoption, extraction accuracy, and reuse across teams.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

  • Resolve and document the MCP audience, governance model, and hand-off point between platform and domain teams

  • Agree a plan and timeline for moving extraction from the existing team onto the shared pipeline

  • Define a sequenced first slice, with baseline metrics for each area

In your first year

  • A versioned public API and Developer Portal that customers integrate with

  • A customer-facing MCP offering live

  • Multiple domain teams extracting from their documents on the shared pipeline, shipping an agent on the agentic layer, without having to run a separate vector store or having to rebuild extraction from scratch

About you

  • 6+ years in product management, with at least 3 on platform, API or developer-facing products in B2B SaaS

  • You've shipped and run public APIs: REST or GraphQL, OAuth and other authentication patterns, versioning, deprecation, and docs developers actually like

  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM features to production, whether extraction, RAG or agents. You understand evaluations, confidence scoring, failure modes and human-in-the-loop review, and can hold your own with Applied AI engineers on chunking, embeddings and model fallback

  • Working knowledge of MCP or agent tool-use, and a clear view on what makes a tool safe and reliable for an agent to call

  • Strong instincts for security and compliance with regulated data: access control, GDPR and data residency

  • You lead through influence. You're comfortable with internal teams as customers and can say no, or not us, clearly and with reasons

  • You write clearly and document decisions so others can build on them

Nice to have

  • Fintech, fund administration or private markets experience: capital calls, capital accounts, subscription documents, LP and portfolio reporting

  • Experience in an EU-regulated environment

  • You've built a Developer Portal or a partner integrations programme from zero

  • You've moved a capability out of one team and into a shared platform without breaking either side

  • Experience in a company moving from ops-led to product-led

Workplace & Benefits

  • Customizable benefits package (wellbeing, sport, mobility, food, and more)

  • 28 days of vacation, plus 2 company days and local public holidays

  • Remote-flexible hybrid (3 days/week in office)

  • Up to 6 remote calendar weeks a year

  • A great tech and work setup

  • Work with a diverse team of 120+ bunchies from 40+ countries, with leaders who are best-in-class in their domains

Hiring process

  1. First interview with the People team (30 min) – Get acquainted with bunch and explore alignment

  2. Hiring Manager Interview with the VP of Product (60 min) – Discuss the role, your experience and your goals

  3. Case Interview with Product & Design (60 min) – Demonstrate how you think, work and communicate, based on a small case shared beforehand

  4. Final meetings with key stakeholders (3 x 30 min) – Learn more about the vision and discuss open questions

Curious to learn more?

Get a feel for who we are, how we work, and what we’re building:

  • About bunch – Our mission, product, and journey so far

  • Case Studies – About those who already build on bunch

  • Gathering insights – Our latest bunch of blog posts

  • Glossary – Explore commonly used private market terms


About bunch

bunch is building the operating infrastructure for the next generation of private markets. We combine AI-powered automation with deep regulatory expertise to replace fragmented spreadsheets and manual processes with one integrated platform across the fund lifecycle, purpose-built for private markets heading toward $32 trillion in Assets Under Management.

We've 4x our ARR in 2025, crossed 150 fund managers and 12,000 LPs on the platform, and just closed our $35M Series B in May 2026. We're looking for ambitious people who want real ownership of hard problems, and who care about building infrastructure that actually matters to the people using it.
